given form, not when it was written, and no independently time-stamped
registration exists. The history is an auditable account, not independent
proof of timing.

An earlier draft stated that the second training seed was prespecified; the
registry names only a conditional three-seed ensemble. The prose plan required
AP/PA, one-image-per-study, concordant-study and uncertain-label sensitivities,
and the machine-readable registry required temperature-scaled and
split-conformal baselines and listed AUGRC as a primary threshold-free metric.
None was run before the results were known. All except the one-image and
concordant-study sensitivities, which need image-level predictions that were
not cached, are reported here post hoc.

\section{Extended methods}\label{ssec:methods}

\paragraph{Cohorts.}
Report sections were extracted with a curated header vocabulary. 66 reports had
no recognised header; 134 merged findings and impression, of which 133 further
studies were removed in the sequential waterfall (199 in total). Tiers were
assigned from the official training split using patient identifiers and a fixed
seed alone; the official validate and test splits were not analysed. At the
external site one study has two images whose context fields differ (one
informative, one not), and one image matches its checksum but does not decode
and was excluded.

\paragraph{Context.}
Source context was the INDICATION and HISTORY sections (registered synonyms);
WET READ, provisional findings, recommendation, notification, addendum and
comment sections are post-diagnostic and never extracted. 17,551 source reports
(7.70\%) contain a WET READ section and 181 place a pre-diagnostic section after
a diagnostic one. Report-section headers occurred in \ScanHeaderSrc{} of the
extracted source contexts and in \ScanHeaderExt{} of the external ones;
conclusion-style phrases in \ScanConclSrc{} and \ScanConclExt{}; comparison
language in \ScanComparSrc{} and \ScanComparExt{}. Effective tokens are
whitespace-delimited tokens with an alphanumeric character after removing runs
of de-identification underscores; N1 requires $\ge T$ ($T=3$ primary). C2
rotates contexts within strata of split and length bin (0--4, 5--9, 10--19,
20--39, 40--79, $\ge$80 tokens), seed 20260718, stepping past same-patient
donors.

\paragraph{Labels.}
The source CheXbert port used the checkpoint published as
\texttt{StanfordAIMI/RRG\_scorers} (SHA-256 \texttt{6550703c\ldots0fde1};
upstream commit \texttt{6d22a96}). Its fidelity check covered 4 public sample reports (56 cells, all matching).
Values are 1, 0, $-1$ (uncertain) or blank (unmentioned). Source labels are
study-level; external labels are image-level and a study takes the first
observed (0/1) value across its frontal images.

\paragraph{Models and training.}
Images were converted to greyscale, resized once to $224\times224$ by bilinear
interpolation without preserving aspect ratio, stored as JPEG (quality 95),
replicated to three channels and ImageNet-normalised, identically at both
sites; no augmentation. M4 concatenates DenseNet-121 pooled features (1,024)
and the BERT CLS embedding (768), then Linear(1792,\,512), ReLU, dropout 0.2 and
Linear(512,\,5). Loss: masked binary cross-entropy averaged over labelled cells
of the batch's images, no weights. AdamW (learning rate $10^{-4}$ image/fusion,
$2\times10^{-5}$ text; weight decay $10^{-4}$), batch 32, fp32, at most 15
epochs, early stopping on internal-validation macro AUROC (patience 3; 5\% of
training patients). Selected checkpoints: M1 epoch 3 (AUROC 0.877), M2 epoch 3
(0.763), M4 epoch 4 (0.888); second seed (20260719): M1 epoch 3 (0.874), M2
epoch 2 (0.768), M4 epoch 1 (0.887).

\paragraph{Frozen policy.}
Thresholds maximise balanced accuracy over $k/1000$, $k=1,\ldots,999$, ties to
the lowest threshold; frozen thresholds ranged from 0.41 to 0.99. The cutoff is
the 20th percentile (linear interpolation) of calibration-study confidence;
studies at or above it are accepted, so ties can push coverage above target.

\paragraph{Estimators.}
With mask $m_{ij}$ (1 for positive or negative), $n_i=\sum_jm_{ij}$,
$w_i=\sum_jm_{ij}\mathbb{1}[\hat y_{ij}\neq y_{ij}]$ and acceptance $a_i$:
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{p{0.24\linewidth}p{0.66\linewidth}}
\toprule
Estimator & Definition\\
\midrule
original (defective) & $\sum_i a_i w_i/\max(n_i,1)\,/\,\sum_i a_i$\\
evaluable-study (corrected) & $\sum_i a_i\mathbb{1}[n_i>0]w_i/n_i\,/\,\sum_i a_i\mathbb{1}[n_i>0]$\\
cell-pooled & $\sum_i a_iw_i/\sum_ia_in_i$\\
pathology-macro & $\frac15\sum_j\sum_ia_im_{ij}\mathbb{1}[\hat y_{ij}\ne y_{ij}]/\sum_ia_im_{ij}$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Label variants change only $m$ and $y$: unmentioned$\to$negative sets blank
cells to observed negatives; uncertain$\to$positive or $\to$negative recodes
$-1$ cells. The uncertain variants were registered in the prose analysis plan;
the unmentioned variant is a post hoc bracket, not a reference standard.

\paragraph{Inference.}
Bootstrap replicates are computed as patient-multiplicity-weighted sums and
replay the original random draws exactly (\cref{ssec:repro}). Multiplicity:
the registry specifies Holm across pathologies, which was not executed before
results; post hoc we report Holm across pathologies and Bonferroni ($k=6$)
intervals for the confirmatory contrasts (\cref{ssec:path}). The power analysis
targeted the minimum detectable effect (0.021--0.027 at 80\% power), not the
materiality. Requiring the point estimate to reach a threshold $\delta$ gives
$\Pr(\text{confirm}\mid\Delta=\delta)=\Pr\{Z\ge\max(0,1.96-\delta/s)\}\le1/2$,
an elementary property of such rules.

cd c3e_audit_toolkit && python -m pytest -q
\end{verbatim}

\section{Expert adjudication protocol (summary)}\label{ssec:adjud}
A blinded adjudication of a stratified sample of studies at both sites is the
analysis that could arbitrate between label-handling alternatives; it has not
been performed. Two board-certified radiologists would label the five findings
from the image alone, blinded to site, report labels and model output, with a
third resolving disagreements. Studies would be sampled within strata of
site $\times$ label availability $\times$ policy decision and estimates weighted
by inverse sampling fractions. About 600 studies per site give a 95\% interval
half-width near 0.05 for per-site error among accepted studies. The full
protocol, form and sample-size table are in the project repository
(\texttt{docs/revision/EXPERT\_ADJUDICATION\_PROTOCOL.md}).
